headline: Harvard Astronomers Capture First Portrait of a Star on Glass Plate
dispatch: Cambridge, Mass., July 18, 1850. William Cranch Bond and John Adams Whipple last night turned the Harvard College Observatory's great refractor on the star Vega and fixed its light upon a daguerreotype plate, producing the first photographic likeness of any star beyond the Sun. The image, a small bright point on silver-coated copper, was clear enough to confirm the method's promise. The achievement opens the prospect of cataloguing the heavens by camera rather than by eye alone.
answer: First daguerreotype of a star (Vega) taken, 1850
